mechanism_narrative: The recent sustained decline in RETAIL_REC mobility, averaging -11.4% over the last four weeks with a low of -17.3%, indicates a persistent trend of reduced discretionary activity that will continue to depress RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: The mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than the mean RETAIL_REC over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES mobility remains below -5% for two consecutive weeks, it signifies a continued reduction in daily commuting and office presence, directly translating to lower weekday foot traffic and thus lower RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES remains below -5% for two consecutive weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days, despite WORKPLACES remaining below -5% for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The simultaneous and sustained increase in RESIDENTIAL mobility (above 5%) and decrease in TRANSIT mobility (below -15%) indicates a strong public preference for staying home and avoiding public transport, which will collectively depress RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days, while RESIDENTIAL mobility remains above 5% and TRANSIT mobility remains below -15%.

mechanism_narrative: The recent rebound in PARKS mobility from -18.9% to -5.3% suggests a renewed willingness for outdoor activity. If this trend continues with another week-on-week increase, it will signal a broader return to local outdoor leisure, leading to a modest increase in RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS shows a week-on-week increase for two consecutive weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is lower than over the last 14 days, despite PARKS showing two consecutive weeks of week-on-week increase.

mechanism_narrative: The sharp spike in GROCERY_PHARM mobility at t-2w (6.6%) followed by its return to baseline (0.0% at t-1w, 0.3% at t-0w) indicates a period of initial panic buying or stocking up. This suggests a temporary reduction in discretionary retail spending as households consume existing supplies, leading to lower RETAIL_REC in the immediate next week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM returns to baseline (within +/-1%) after a spike above 5%.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC in the next week is higher than the average RETAIL_REC of the last week, given GROCERY_PHARM returned to baseline after a spike.

mechanism_narrative: The widespread and concurrent decline across RETAIL_REC, TRANSIT, and WORKPLACES, alongside a significant increase in RESIDENTIAL mobility, collectively indicates an effective, likely policy-driven, encouragement for people to stay home. This will continue to suppress RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days, while TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain significantly depressed and RESIDENTIAL remains elevated.

mechanism_narrative: The stabilization of WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility at significantly reduced levels (around -7% and -20% respectively) over the last two weeks suggests a new, lower equilibrium for daily commuting. This sustained reduction in movement will keep RETAIL_REC suppressed over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain within 3 percentage points of their t-0w values for two consecutive weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is higher than over the last 14 days, despite WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remaining stable at their reduced levels.

mechanism_narrative: After three consecutive weeks of elevated RESIDENTIAL mobility (above 5%), a saturation point may be reached where individuals seek minor local excursions for mental well-being, leading to a slight rebound in RETAIL_REC, particularly for local and essential retail, over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL mobility remains above 5% for three consecutive weeks and shows no further significant increase (less than 1% week-on-week change).
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days, even if RESIDENTIAL mobility remains high and stable as described.
